correctness.rationale: For f(S)=(−1)^|S|, its Boolean Möbius transform at C is the binomial sum (−2)^|C|. Every subset of A∩B is retained by downward closure, so the exact integral congruence is H=Z diag((−2)^|C|) Zᵀ with Z the unit lower-triangular incidence matrix. Unimodularity, changing signs and sorting by cardinality give the divisibility chain 2^|C|. The same congruence gives the signed determinant and Sylvester inertia. Multiplying the two Boolean inverse-zeta entries and summing over C⊇A∪B gives the stated inverse, including its sign. Invertible basis changes persist modulo 2^r; the one-coordinate kernel of 2^k has 2^min(k,r) elements. All factors are units modulo odd integers, and at n=0 the singleton ideal gives [1].
residual_risks: The frozen verifier's lines 38–40 only calculate a predicted kernel size and assert it is positive; they do not check actual modular kernels despite the supporting description. The proof, not those lines, establishes the modular claim.
The result does not cover arbitrary principal subsets, distinct row and column supports, or numerical conditioning.

evidence: Korkee 2004 quotes the general inverse for meet-closed sets, using the inverse zeta and the Möbius transform in its denominator. Every Boolean ideal in the finding is meet-closed.
The lower-ideal incidence congruence is the standard zeta expansion of an arbitrary f of a meet; the entries of Z are integral with determinant one.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For a lower ideal the denominator in (3.22) is just the Möbius transform at x_k: a proper element below x_k already occurs earlier in the linear extension. The general inverse reduces to the exact frozen formula, and the same congruence supplies the other invariants.

originality.rationale: The principal Walsh matrix is exactly a classical meet matrix: take the Boolean meet-semilattice, the downward-closed family, and the weight f(S)=(−1)^|S|. The standard integral incidence factorization and meet-matrix inverse specialize with the single binomial transform (−2)^|C|. Because those diagonal moduli already divide one another in face order, the Smith and modular conclusions require no additional structural theorem about Walsh matrices.
residual_risks: Full text of Hacıoğlu and of Haukkanen's 1996 On meet matrices on posets was not obtained. The decisive general inverse was read in Korkee's open paper and the broader incidence implication was checked mathematically. The failure does not depend on the inaccessible texts.

value.rationale: The exact modular sample count is useful information, but in this scope it is a routine coordinatewise consequence of a classical incidence diagonalization specialized by the binomial theorem. The finding does not address stability, unequal row and column supports, or another nonmechanical sampling invariant.
residual_risks: The failure is for the research value of the original claim, not the correctness or pedagogical usefulness of the Fourier example.
